title: World Aquatics moving 2 World Cup events out of Canada over stance on Russia, Belarus in international sports
summary: The world governing body for aquatic sports has decided to move a pair of events out of Canada due to the federal government's stance that Russian and Belarusian athletes can't enter the country…

image.caption: A general view during the World Aquatics Diving World Cup 2026 stop at Centre Sportif Du Parc Olympique on Feb. 28 in Montreal. The 2027 World Cup event has been relocated from Montreal to Mexico. (Getty Images)

blocks.text: The world governing body for aquatic sports has decided to move a pair of events out of Canada due to the federal government's stance that Russian and Belarusian athletes can't enter the country unless they compete as neutral athletes.
Sporting body cites statements made by Canadian government about Russian, Belarusian athletes
World Aquatics said in a statement on Saturday that World Cup diving and World Cup artistic swimming events set to be held in Montreal in early 2027 will not be happening in the city.

They acknowledge "recent statements made by the Canadian government, which make it clear that Russian and Belarusian athletes, unless competing as neutral under their conditions, would not be allowed to enter Canada to participate in scheduled competitions," the statement read.

After discussions with stakeholders, World Aquatics has moved the opening stop of the diving World Cup in February 2027 from Montreal to Mexico. The artistic swimming World Cup event in April 2027 will be removed from the competition calendar while they decide on a new host.
"World Aquatics remains committed to fostering inclusive and universally accessible international competition free from political intervention," the statement continued.

"World Aquatics appreciates the constructive engagement of Aquatics Canada and its member federations throughout this process. We value our longstanding hosting relationship with Canada and look forward to returning to Canada for future World Aquatics events."

blocks.text: Diving Plongeon Canada (DPC) responded to World Aquatics decision, expressing "disappointment" of the Montreal event being moved.

"DPC acknowledges World Aquatics' decision to revise the international competition schedule in response to the Canadian government's position that Russian and Belarusian athletes, unless competing as neutral athletes, would not be permitted to enter Canada to participate in scheduled competitions," the organization said in a released statement.

"Diving Plongeon Canada also recognizes the Canadian government's position regarding the participation of Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials in international sporting events hosted in Canada. While this decision is beyond DPC’s control, we recognize the great disappointment it brings to our athletes, partners and the entire Canadian diving community, who were looking forward to welcoming the world's best divers to Canada, as we have since 2014."
Earlier this month, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Russian and Belarusian athletes will not be permitted to represent their countries in Canada as long as the war in Ukraine continues.

While Russia and Belarus are "supporting this illegal, unjustified, horrific war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," Carney said when asked if Russian hockey players would be denied visas for the world junior hockey championships happening in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta., next month.
With files from Myles Dichter and CBC Sports
